title: Illustration / Isometric style — Design

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Keep perspective, light and material cues coherent so viewers can understand spatial relationships without visual contradictions.
strategic_value: A common isometric construction and restrained lighting can help IBM explain complex technology while retaining a sense of clarity and ease.
demonstration: Spatial scenes are followed by primitive volumes, grid and angle construction, curve and radius examples, surface treatments and consistent versus conflicting shadows.
practical_value: Choose isometric illustration when depth aids explanation, then keep grid alignment, light direction and shadow style consistent.

content_islands.name: Spatial examples
content_islands.spec: Introduce technology and human scenes with floating, thin and aligned objects.

content_islands.name: Volumes and behavior
content_islands.spec: Show primitive solid families and their combination into a magnifying glass and book, followed by lightweight arrangements.

content_islands.name: Grid and construction
content_islands.spec: Present the isometric grid, snapped-point comparisons, a laptop construction overlay and predefined angle diagram.

content_islands.name: Curves and nested geometry
content_islands.spec: Compare circular and organic curves and aligned human forms, then nested radii.

content_islands.name: Materials and illumination
content_islands.spec: Finish with gradients, transparency, single-source lighting and shadow-style comparisons, ending with an illuminated layered graphic.

ingredient.name: Isometric perspective and lighting
ingredient.role: Make spatial and material relationships readable.
ingredient.application: Ground primary objects in the isometric grid; use a single consistent light direction and a consistent shadow style within an illustration or related set.
ingredient.scope: IBM isometric illustrations. Organic curves are permitted but retain an isometric foundation; transparency is added only when necessary.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source recommends isometric style when space and dimension improve explanation and connects lightweight arrangements to ease in human–technology relationships.
reference_purposes.Expression: The illustrated scenes demonstrate IBM’s spatial technology vocabulary.
reference_purposes.Application: Grid, volume and light diagrams explain how to construct and shade the style.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source directs primary elements to isometric angles, requires a consistent single light source and shadow style, and permits off-grid anchors only when necessary.
